text:
sophia: Quick heads-up: we're introducing a "gradual overage throttle" next Wednesday to reduce surprise invoices from accidental traffic spikes. It will apply soft pacing on sustained outlier usage with clear headers and invoice guidance. Draft: https://redwood.internal/policies/overage-throttles

michael: Will this affect enterprise customers with committed capacity?

sophia: Committed capacity customers are protected by contract; throttles only kick in for PAYG and free-tier accounts unless a pool-level emergency occurs.

finance-bot: Billing note: tokens generated are billed as usual. If the throttle causes a system-side failed completion, file a ticket and we will evaluate credits case-by-case.

support: Adding quick KB and canned responses now. We'll surface X-Redwood-Overage-Throttle: true in responses so SDKs can detect and backoff.

ops-bot: Canary rollout scheduled Thu 08:00 PT -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 36h. Monitoring: throttle_events/min, p99 latency, failed_completions. Auto-abort on SLO regressions.

michael: Suggested public wording = "temporary request pacing for unusually large bursts to keep latency stable across customers". Keep "overage" out of public copy.

sophia: Agreed. Final: "temporary request pacing to protect latency and reduce unexpected charges from accidental spikes." Thanks — publishing doc + customer emails tomorrow. :rocket:
